title: What If the Large Hadron Collider Made a Black Hole?

scenes.text: What if the Large Hadron Collider made a black hole? Physicists have already answered it.
Under Einstein's gravity, the collider can't make one. A few speculative theories say it could, but only microscopic ones.
Those theories agree such a black hole would fall apart instantly, with no time to grow or swallow anything.
Each proton collision carries about as much energy as a flying mosquito.
And nature has already run the experiment. Cosmic rays have produced roughly a million LHC-equivalent collisions on Earth over its history.
Neutron stars and white dwarfs, hit by even more cosmic rays, are still here. A safety review endorsed by physics societies concluded the collider is safe.

description:
What if the Large Hadron Collider made a black hole?
CERN's safety review says it can't, and if exotic theories were right, the black hole would vanish instantly. Cosmic rays have already run the experiment a million times over.
What should we run through next?
